caseno: Writ Petition No. 4005 of 1992 with Writ Petition No. 4102 of 1992
lawyer:
Shamsul Hoque Chowdhury with Ozair Farruq and Shamsun Nahar, Advocates — For the Petitioners
Md. Saidur Rahman, Assistant Attorney General— For the Respondent No. 2. 
K S Zaman, Advocate — For the Respondent No.3.
parties:
Shah (Md) ----- Petitioner (In Writ Petition]
Vs.
Secretary to the President, People's Republic of Bangladesh & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
5. Mr. Mohammad Shah, the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 4005 of 1992 and Mr. Md. Abdul Malek, the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 4102, of 1992 were working as Assistant Engineers, the House Building Finance Corporation, the Managing Director of which has been made the respondent No. 3. The House Building Finance Corporation is a statutory corporation under the administrative control of the Ministry of Finance. After the proclamation of Martial Law on the 24th March 1982 the Constitution was suspended and after promulgating the Proclamation of 24th March, 1982 many other Martial Law Proclamations. Martial Law Orders, Chief Martial Law Administrator's Orders, Martial Law Regulations, etc. were promulgated and given effect to in supersession of the Constitution. The Chief Martial Law Administrator also promulgated Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 on the 6th of April, 1982 which vested the Chief Martial Law Administrator with the power to remove any person. 

 6. On the 10th December, 1985, the Chief Martial Law Administrator by an order constituted an Enquiry Committee directing that the said Enquiry Committee should consist of a Chairman who is the Respondent No. 4 of this writ petition and an officer of the rank of Superintending Engineer to be nominated by the House Building Finance Corporation and an officer of the rank of Superintending Engineer to be nominated by the Chief Engineer of the Public Works Department and an officer of the rank of Accounts Officer of an appropriate status to be nominated by the Chairman, Dhaka Improvement Trust, to inquire into certain illegalities, irregularities, etc. regarding grant and disbursement of loans by the House Building Finance Corporation. It is alleged by the petitioners that the above Committee was constituted in violation of the above order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator as none of the members was holding the position of Superintending Engineer and one of the members, who has been made the Respondent No. 5 in these Writ Petitions was a Sub-Divisional Engineer and another member who has been made the respondent No. 6 in these writ petitions was an Assistant Engineer holding current charge of the Executive Engineer. This committee was specially enjoined to hold enquiry into certain illegalities in granting of house building loan, etc. by the House Building Finance Corporation in Tangail area, after constitution of this committee both the petitioners received intimation from a Deputy General Manager (operation) of the House Building Finance Corporation asking them to appear before the enquiry committee. They appeared before the Enquiry Committee and it is alleged that the said Committee adopted the procedure as prescribed under the Bangladesh Army Act and did not hold any enquiry according to rules or procedures governing the civil officers. It is also alleged that violating the rules and normal procedures the said Enquiry Committee put the petitioners under duress and threat and then interrogated them and arbitrarily recorded some answers purported to have been given by the petitioners and treated these answers as admission. It is also alleged that the Enquiry Committee then submitted fraudulent report to the Chief Martial Law Administrator and the Chief Martial Law Administrator removed the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 4005 of 1992 by an order passed on 17.4.1986 under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 and removed the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 4102 of 1992, by another order passed on the same date under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982. 

 7. Thereafter, the petitioners submitted several petitions addressed to the Chief Martial Law Administrator for reviewing the above orders of removal but no order was passed. Then, on the basis of a decision of this Court reported in 42 DLR 1, in the case of Mahtabuddin Ahmed vs. Principal Secretary, President's Secretariat, Dhaka and others, the President of Bangladesh created a forum for review after the withdrawal of Martial Law and restoration of the Constitution on the 10th November, 1986 This forum for review took up the applications of the petitioners for review and after reviewing decided to uphold the order of removal of the petitioners passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator on 7th April, 1986 and communicated this decision to the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 4005 of 1992 by the impugned letter as at Annexure-J to the Writ Petition and to the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 4102 of 1992 by the impugned Annexure-J thereof. 

 9. Mr. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the cases, has urged before us that the Enquiry Committee was constituted in complete disregard and after contravention of the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator inasmuch as instead of constituting the Committee with two officers of the rank of Superintending Engineer, the Committee was illegally constituted with two members holding the post of Assistant Engineers and, as such, said Enquiry Committee was coram non-judice, He has also submitted that since pursuant to the report of the said illegally constituted Enquiry Committee the Chief Martial Law Administrator passed the impugned order under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 on 17th April, 1986, removing the petitioners from service, the said order was illegal and without lawful authority. He has also urged that the Review Committee which considered the application for review filed by the petitioners did not take into consideration the above illegality committed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator in depending on the report of the illegally constituted Committee and illegally upheld the orders of the Chief Martial Law Administrator and, as such, neither the decision of the Review Committee conveyed to the petitioner by Annexure-J to the writ petition nor the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator passed under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 can be sustained and must be held to be without lawful authority. 

 10. Mr. Md. Saidur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, representing the respondent No. 2 in both the writ petitions, has contended that the orders passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 are protected by paragraph 19 of the 4th Schedule to the Constitution enacted by the Constitution (7th Amendment) Act, 1986, and, as such, said order cannot be called in question by any court. He has also contended that after considering all the materials before it and after hearing the petitioners the forum for review did not find any ground to disturb the order passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator and, as such, decided to uphold the said order of removal of the petitioners from service. 

 13. Mr. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury, has, first of all, challenged the constitution of the Enquiry Committee and in support of his submission, he has filed a copy of the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator where-by the Chief Martial Law Administrator passed the order for constituting the Enquiry Committee. The copy of the said order is at Annexure-A to the writ petition. It shows that the Chief Martial Law Administrator constituted the Enquiry Committee as follows: 

 2. 1 X-Officer of the rank of Superintending Engineer to be nominated, by the Chief Engineer, PWD. 

 14. It has been alleged by the petitioners in their respective petitions that ignoring the above order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator two Assistant Engineers instead of two Superintending Engineers were included in the Enquiry Committee as members. These allegations made in the writ petitions have not been denied or challenged or nothing has been produced before us to show that the allegations are not correct. It therefore, appears that contrary to the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator, two members were nominated in the Committee from among Assistant Engineers instead of Superintending Engineers. As such, it appears that Mr. Shamsul Huq Chowdhury was correct while he submitted that the said Committee was not constituted according to the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator. 

 15. Mr. Chowdhury has then referred to the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator passed under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 whereby the petitioners were removed from service. The orders of the Chief Martial Law Administrator are at Annexure-F respectively to the two writ petitions. These orders show that the Chief Martial Law Administrator was of opinion that the removal of both the petitioners from service was necessary in the interest of the government and therefore in exercise of his powers conferred by Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 he was pleased to dismiss the petitioners from the House Building Finance Corporation with immediate effect. 

 "19 (2) All orders made, acts and things done and actions and proceedings taken, purported to have been made, done or taken, by the President or the Chief Martial Law Administrator or by any other person or authority during the said period, in exercise or purported exercise of the powers derived from the said Proclamation Order, Chief Martial Law Administrator's Order, Martial Law Regulation, Martial Law Order, Martial Law Instruction, Ordinance or any other Law made or sentence passed by any court, tribunal or authority in the exercise or purported exercise of such powers, shall be deemed to have been validly made, done or taken and shall not be called in question in or before any court, tribunal or authority on any ground whatsoever." 

 17. Sub-paragraph (2) of paragraph 19 shows that all orders made, acts and things done, and actions and proceedings taken, or purported to have been made, done or taken, by the President or the Chief Martial Law Administrator or any authority during the period of Martial Law in exercise or purported exercise of powers derived from the said Proclamation or from any other Proclamation, Proclamation Order, Chief Martial Law Administrator's Order Martial Law Regulation, Martial Law Order, Martial Law Instruction, Martial Law Ordinance, etc. would be deemed to have been validly made, done or taken and would not be called in question in or before any court, tribunal or authority on any ground whatsoever." 

 19. It, therefore, appears that although the Chief Martial Law Administrator may have acted on the report of a Committee not properly constituted, passed the impugned orders of dismissal under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 on 17.4.1988 and, as such, these orders were protected by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1986 and could not be called in question in any court including this Court. So, the jurisdiction of this court to call in question the said order is ousted. 

 20. Mr. Chowdhury has referred to us the case of Mahtabuddin Ahmed vs Principal Secretary, President's Secretariat & ors reported in 42 DLR 1 and has argued that in the said case this Court issued a direction on the President after withdrawal of Martial Law to create a forum for disposing of the applications for review filed by persons affected by Orders under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 and as a result of the said decision various forums for review were created and various orders of removal passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator or under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 wen, reviewed and many persons were reinstated in service. 

 21. We have carefully considered this decision. In this decision it was not held that the order passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator under Martial Law Order No. 9 was subject to review by this Court. It was not held in that case that the orders passed under Martial Law Order No. 9 could be reopened for review by this court. The ratio decidendi in that case is that paragraph 1(a) of the Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 conferred a right on the affected person to get an order passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 reviewed and, as such, if any application for review filed by any affected person was pending on the date or withdrawal of Martial Law the affected person's right to have his application for review decided subsisted and accordingly, direction was issued to create a forum for disposing of the application for review filed by the petitioner which still remained undecided. In the present case also, in pursuance of the said case the government created a forum for disposing of the applications filed by the petitioners for reviewing the orders passed by the Chief Martial Law Administrator. This court can, however, examine whether the forum for review created for reviewing the orders passed in respect of the present petitioners by the Chief Martial Law Administrator under Martial Law Order, No. 9 of 1982 followed the proper procedures and while deciding the applications for review of the petitioners the principles of natural justice were observed by the said forum. 

 22. It appears from the letter whereby the decisions of the forum for review were conveyed to the petitioners as at Annexure-J respectively to both the writ petitions that the said forum examined the applications for review respectively filed by the petitioners, the connected papers and the reports of the Enquiry Committee and have also heard both the petitioners in person and thereafter on the basis of the materials before it came to the conclusion that the petitioners could not prove before the forum that they were not guilty and, as such, the forum for review found that there was no reason to disturb the orders of the Chief Martial Law Administrator. 

 24. It, therefore, appears that in absence of any rules or procedures prescribed for the forum for review to be followed the forum for review adopted its own procedure and on the basis of the materials produced before it and also after affording the petitioners an opportunity of being heard came to the impugned decisions in respect of the two petitioners. We cannot enter into the merits or propriety of the decision arrived at by the forum for review. In our writ jurisdiction we can only see whether the procedures adopted by the forum for review were reasonable and whether the principles of natural justice were observed by it and whether the petitioners were afforded proper opportunity of placing their case before it. We have found that the procedure adopted by the forum for review were reasonable procedures in absence of any prescribed rules. We therefore, do not find any reason to interfere with the decisions of the forum for review as conveyed to the petitioners as at Annexure-J of both the writ petitions and also with the order of the Chief Martial Law Administrator passed under Martial Law Order No. 9 of 1982 whereby the petitioners were removed from service.
